body:
bcrypt 13 is too aggressive we should be suggesting bcrypt 10.

https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/Password_Storage_Cheat_Sheet.html

comments.body:
This refers to 2.4.4, not 2.2.4:

[2.4.4 Verify that if bcrypt is used, the work factor SHOULD be as large as verification server performance will allow, typically at least 13.](https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/blob/master/4.0/en/0x11-V2-Authentication.md#:~:text=verify%20that%20if%20bcrypt%20is%20used%2C%20the%20work%20factor%20should%20be%20as%20large%20as%20verification%20server%20performance%20will%20allow%2C%20typically%20at%20least%2013)

Work factors correspond to time roughly like this, on my laptop:

| bcrypt | time |
|--------|------------|
| 10     | 50 ms         |
| 11     | 100 ms        |
| 12     | 200 ms        |
| 13     | 400 ms        |

I think 10 is acceptable. I agree that 13 is a bit much.
This has been updated for a different issue making this issue moot.
